title: Bound process-local Multi-Site health registry state by Site cardinality

opportunity.rootCause: SiteHealthRegistry retained one state entry and one weighted-round-robin cursor per Site in unbounded concurrent dictionaries; repeated Site creation/deletion could grow process memory indefinitely.
opportunity.scope: SiteHealthRegistry legacy/manual health state and upstream selection

implementation: Replaced unbounded per-key concurrent dictionaries with a lock-protected bounded Site bucket registry and configurable maxSites defaulting to 1024.
Added monotonic recency tracking and least-recently-used eviction when a new Site bucket would exceed the global bound.
Kept per-upstream health state, reason truncation, unknown-upstream behavior, and weighted round-robin selection semantics intact.

tddRed.reason: The new bounded-registry test initially could not compile because SiteHealthRegistry had no maxSites constructor parameter (CS1739).

boundaries: Long-running memory benchmark with thousands of live Sites
Live PostgreSQL-backed legacy health execution and concurrent multi-instance behavior
CodeQL/SARIF, external penetration testing, load/SLO, SIEM, Authenticode signing, and production certification
